title: the override settings are read only at import, so a changed file needs a new session
author: Claude-JG
description: The maintainer, testing 1.12.95 in Spyder: the settings file is only picked up after restarting the console, which makes storing something look as if it had not worked. 'import exudyn' reads the file once, and a second import of an already imported module does nothing, so a file written by the store button - or edited by hand - has no effect until the interpreter is restarted. Spyder keeps the kernel, which is where this is met. Wanted: a function that re-reads the file into exudyn.special.overrideSettings and applies what can be applied at once, so that a session can pick up what it has just stored, and a line in the documentation saying which settings need a restart and why. One thing to decide in the step: the subclasses that apply the visualizationSettings to every new structure are installed at import and ONLY when the file holds such a section, so a reload cannot make them appear - either they are installed whenever the file could hold one, or the reload installs them, or the documentation says that this part needs a restart. revision2026b step RG12.14.
releaseNotes: exudyn.misc.overrideSettings.Reload() reads ~/.exudyn/config.json again into exudyn.special.overrideSettings and applies what can be applied, so a file edited while a session runs - or stored by another session - takes effect without restarting the interpreter. That is the Spyder case: import exudyn reads the file once and importing an already imported module does nothing, which made a stored setting look as if it had not been stored. The store is emptied first, so a section removed from the file is gone from it; the config section is applied; and the visualizationSettings reach every structure created afterwards - INCLUDING the case where the file had none at import, which is when the reload is what installs the wrapped constructors. A reload does not undo: a setting that already reached exudyn.config, and a structure that already exists, keep what they were given, and that is documented. The step was much smaller than it was raised, because the maintainer noticed that StoreSection already updates the store as well as the file, and because the wrappers close over that same dictionary - so a store already takes effect in its own session. Three tests and the documentation of the workflow under the Exudyn module.
